text: Two old credential problems have been sitting on Dante's backlog: grain-ingest's Azure SQL login, stored as a Kubernetes Secret, and a years-old AWS access key baked into Fairmont's nightly settlement-export job.

This video replaces both with identity instead of secrets. On Azure, Workload Identity federates grain-ingest's own service account to a managed identity scoped to exactly db_datareader and db_datawriter — no broader role, no shared password.
On AWS, an IAM role attached through an EC2 instance profile replaces the static key, scoped to one S3 prefix only.
Neither workload's actual logic changes. The old SQL Secret and the old AWS key are both removed once each cutover is confirmed working end to end.
What changes is that nothing either workload uses to prove who it is can be copied, leaked, or left in a config file again.
